summary: Advises network administrators to remove old filters that blocked traffic or BGP routes from IPv4 /8 blocks that were once unallocated. Now that no unallocated /8s remain, such filters are fragile and costly. It lists the IPv4 prefixes that should still not be routed across the public Internet. It is a best current practice.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 6441 advises network operators to remove old filters for IPv4 /8 blocks that were once unallocated. Those blocks can now carry legitimate traffic, so the old filters may block it by mistake.

subtitle: Guidance to remove IPv4 filters based on address allocation status.

tldr.problem: Now that no IPv4 /8 blocks remain unallocated, filters based on allocation status are more complex and can block legitimate traffic.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC says network operators SHOULD remove ingress and egress packet filters and BGP prefix filters for previously unallocated IPv4 /8s. It distinguishes these from filters for Martian prefixes.
tldr.outcome: RFC 6441 is a Best Current Practice and advises against filtering traffic solely because an address block's registration status was previously unallocated.

today: RFC 6441 is a Best Current Practice. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Allocation-Based Filters Should Go
sections.content: Network administrators have filtered IP traffic and BGP prefixes from unallocated IPv4 address space. The RFC says there are no longer any unallocated IPv4 /8s, so legitimate Internet traffic can come from all unicast /8s that are not reserved for special purposes. Filters based on registration status have become more complicated, fragile, and expensive.
sections.plainLanguage: Previously unallocated address blocks can now be used for legitimate traffic. A filter that still blocks them based on their old status can block that traffic.

sections.title: What Operators Should Remove
sections.content: Network operators SHOULD remove ingress and egress packet filters, as well as BGP prefix filters, for previously unallocated IPv4 /8s. Administrators who continue to filter unallocated IPv4 addresses managed by Regional Internet Registries need more detailed ingress filters and must update them daily to avoid blocking legitimate traffic.
sections.plainLanguage: Remove packet and route filters that rely on the former unallocated status of IPv4 /8 blocks. Keeping more detailed filters requires daily updates to avoid blocking legitimate traffic.

sections.title: Reserved Prefixes and Other Security
sections.content: The RFC says operators may filter traffic destined for Martian prefixes, whose table is defined by RFC 5735. Any change to that table would be documented in an RFC updating or obsoleting RFC 5735. Removing allocation-status filters does not remove the need for other security solutions; the RFC says those remain necessary.
sections.plainLanguage: Removing these filters does not remove other security protections. Operators may still filter prefixes reserved for special use.
